The promise: a NEW game = a new data MODULE, no engine changes. We are EMPIRICALLY testing that promise: for a game of a COMPLETELY different focus than crime-detective, would you truly need only a module, or would you ALSO keep changing the engine? Be concrete and skeptical — trace actual registries/contracts, don't take the claim on faith. PROBE GENRE 1 — "Peaceful Trading Village" (economy sim, ZERO crime/justice): NPCs produce/buy/sell goods, accumulate wealth, set prices, compete on trade, form business rivalries — NO murder, NO arrest, NO judge. Trace concretely what this game needs and whether each is module-only or forces an engine change. Consider: event types (TRADE/PRICE_CHANGE/GOODS_PRODUCED), affordances (haggle/produce/undercut), MOTIVATION (profit/greed — does volition/PM/instinct support a non-crime motive cleanly?), CONSEQUENCES (does CG generalize to economic ripple effects, or does it assume crime?), STATE (inventory/ownership/wealth — does agent-state/beliefs support this or is it missing?), GOALS (accumulate-wealth goal steps). For each need: moduleOnly (which registry) OR forcedEngineChange (with reason + classification: new-universal-capability vs crime-assumption-leak). Give a per-genre verdict + confidence. Read the engine subsystems to ground each claim.
